correctness.rationale: PASS. The classification can be reconstructed directly from the two primitive diagonal idempotents. If a graded involution fixes them, anti-multiplicativity forces \(e_{12}^*=a e_{21}\) and \(e_{21}^*=a^{-1}e_{12}\), giving the family \(\sigma_a\). If it swaps them, the off-diagonal matrix units are fixed up to one common sign, giving exactly \(\rho_+\) and \(\rho_-\). Graded automorphisms normalize the diagonal algebra and are monomial; diagonal conjugation changes \(a\) by a square and the permutation matrix replaces \(a\) by \(a^{-1}\), so square classes are exactly the diagonal-fixing isomorphism invariant. In characteristic zero, after adjoining \(\sqrt{a/b}\), \(\sigma_a\) and \(\sigma_b\) become graded-isomorphic. Multilinearization and restriction/scalar extension then give equality of their graded-star identity ideals and graded-star central-polynomial spaces.
